content: 1. Phenobarbital affects the metabolism of hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Phenobarbital and oxazepam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Phenobarbital decreases oxcarbazepine levels by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 4. Belladonna alkaloids and oxybutynin both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Monitor closely. 5. Phenobarbital decreases oxybutynin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 6. Belladonna alkaloids and oxybutynin topical both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Belladonna alkaloids and oxybutynin transdermal both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Phenobarbital decreases oxycodone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Phenobarbital and oxycodone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Phenobarbital and oxymorphone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Phenobarbital decreases ozanimod levels by other mechanisms (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of ozanimod with strong CYP2C8 inducers reduces the exposure of its active metabolites (CC112273 and CC1084037), potentially decreasing its efficacy. Co-administration with strong CYP2C8 inducers is not recommended. 11. Phenobarbital decreases paclitaxel levels by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and other mechanisms (see comment). Use caution and monitor closely. Paclitaxel levels and efficacy may decrease when co-administered with CYP2C8 inducers. 12. Phenobarbital decreases paclitaxel protein-bound levels by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and other mechanisms (see comment). Use caution and monitor closely. Paclitaxel protein-bound levels and efficacy may decrease when co-administered with CYP2C8 inducers. 13. Phenobarbital decreases palbociclib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A inducers reduce palbociclib plasma exposure by approximately 85%. 14. Belladonna alkaloids decrease paliperidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Belladonna alkaloids also decrease paliperidone levels by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital decreases paliperidone levels by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Phenobarbital and paliperidone both increase sedation. Paliperidone increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. 15. Phenobarbital decreases palovarotene levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Belladonna alkaloids and pancuronium both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Phenobarbital decreases pancuronium effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 17. Phenobarbital decreases panobinostat levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. 18. Phenobarbital decreases pantoprazole levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 19. Phenobarbital and papaveretum both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Phenobarbital and papaverine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Phenobarbital decreases parecoxib levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 22. Phenobarbital decreases paromomycin levels by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Passion flower increases the effects of phenobarbital by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination may enhance central nervous system (CNS) depression. 24. Phenobarbital decreases pazopanib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Phenobarbital decreases pemigatinib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Phenobarbital decreases penbutolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration of phenobarbital. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. 27. Phenobarbital and pentazocine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Pentobarbital and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Phenobarbital decreases perampanel levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Perphenazine increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and perphenazine both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids decrease perphenazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. 31. Phenobarbital decreases pexidartinib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Phenobarbital increases and phendimetrazine decreases sedation. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 33. Phenelzine increases phenobarbital levels by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 34. Phenobarbital decreases phenindione effects by increasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Phenobarbital increases and phentermine decreases sedation. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 36. Phenobarbital increases and phenylephrine decreases sedation. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 37. Phenobarbital decreases phenytoin levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Phenobarbital may occasionally not change or even increase phenytoin levels via competitive inhibition. 38. Phenobarbital and pholcodine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Physostigmine increases and belladonna alkaloids decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 40. Pilocarpine increases and belladonna alkaloids decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 41. Phenobarbital decreases pimavanserin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible. Monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy. An increase in pimavanserin dosage may be needed. 42. Pimozide increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Belladonna alkaloids decrease pimozide levels by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital and pimozide both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids decrease pimozide levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. 43. Phenobarbital decreases pindolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration of phenobarbital. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. 44. Phenobarbital decreases pioglitazone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 45. Phenobarbital increases and pirbuterol decreases sedation. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 46. Phenobarbital decreases pirfenidone levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Use of strong CYP1A2 inducers should be discontinued before initiating pirfenidone and avoided during treatment. 47. Phenobarbital decreases piroxicam levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 48. Phenobarbital decreases pirtobrutinib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Phenobarbital decreases pitolisant levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pitolisant exposure is decreased by 50% if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If the strong CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, reduce pitolisant dosage by half. 50. Phenobarbital decreases polatuzumab vedotin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer may decrease unconjugated MMAE AUC. 51. Phenobarbital decreases pomalidomide levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Phenobarbital decreases ponatinib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug unless the co-administration outweighs the possible risk of ponatinib underexposure. Monitor for signs of reduced efficacy. 53. Phenobarbital decreases posaconazole levels by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by increasing metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 54. Belladonna alkaloids and pralidoxime both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Phenobarbital decreases pralsetinib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unable to avoid, double the current pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of co-administration with a strong CYP3A inducer. After the inducer has been discontinued for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. 56. Pramlintide and belladonna alkaloids increase each other's effects by pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is contraindicated due to synergistic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. 57. Phenobarbital decreases praziquantel levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 58. Phenobarbital decreases prednisolone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Phenobarbital decreases prednisone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Phenobarbital decreases pretomanid levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate. Avoid co-administration of strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 61. Phenobarbital decreases primaquine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Phenobarbital and primidone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Procarbazine increases phenobarbital levels by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 64. Belladonna alkaloids decrease prochlorperazine levels by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Prochlorperazine increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and prochlorperazine both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids decrease prochlorperazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. 65. Phenobarbital decreases progesterone intravaginal gel levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 66. Phenobarbital decreases progesterone micronized levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 67. Phenobarbital decreases natural progesterone levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
